title: Vehicles
description:
Build a small hierarchy.

`Vehicle` (the base):
- `Vehicle(std::string name, int wheels)`
- `const std::string& name() const`, `int wheels() const`
- `std::string describe() const` returns for example `"Civic has 4 wheels"`

`Car` (derived from `Vehicle`):
- `Car(std::string name, int doors)`: always 4 wheels
- `int doors() const`

`Motorbike` (derived from `Vehicle`):
- `explicit Motorbike(std::string name)`: always 2 wheels
- `bool hasSidecar() const` (false until `attachSidecar()` is called, which also makes `wheels()` report 3)

For the sidecar, `Vehicle` needs a way for derived classes (but not outsiders) to change the wheel count: give it a **protected** `void setWheels(int)`.
hints: Derived constructors pass their part up in the initializer list: `Car(std::string name, int doors) : Vehicle{ std::move(name), 4 }, m_doors{ doors } {}`.
For the sidecar, give `Vehicle` a `protected` function (such as `setWheels(int)`) that `Motorbike::attachSidecar` can call but outside code cannot.
